title: The Alchemy of Happiness
author: Al-Ghazali (Field trans)
description: The Alchemy of Happiness (Kimiya-yi Sa'adat) by Abu Hamid al-Ghazali (1058-1111), translated by Claud Field (London: John Murray, Wisdom of the East series, 1910), an abridged English version made from the Hindustani. Al-Ghazali, the great Persian theologian whose spiritual crisis led him to Sufism, wrote this Persian summary of his monumental Revival of the Religious Sciences for a broader readership. It teaches that true happiness, the alchemy that transforms base metal into gold, is attained through knowledge of the self, of God, of this world and of the next. Chapters explain the heart as a mirror to be polished, the struggle with passions, the love of God as the highest end, music and ecstasy, self-examination and remembrance of death. Field's version introduces the ethical and mystical core of al-Ghazali's thought and its reconciliation of law, theology and Sufism.
